examples.en: On Lunar New Year's Day, I wear a hanbok with my family.
I rented a hanbok at Gyeongbokgung.
There are many hanbok shops in front of Gyeongbokgung.

examples.ko: 한복은 비싸요? — 아니요, 하루에 삼만 원이에요.
examples.en: Is hanbok expensive? — No, it's 30,000 won a day.

explain: 한복은 ‘한(韓, 한국) + 복(服, 옷)’이에요. 요즘은 명절이나 결혼식 같은 날에 입는 사람이 많아요.

dict_examples.en: To have a set of hanbok made and wear it.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: To dress up neatly in hanbok.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: 한복 is 한 (韓, Korea) + 복 (服, clothes). Today many people wear it on holidays and at weddings.

examples.en: It's already nine in the evening.
I want to become an actor someday.

examples.ko: 제 딸은 내년에 스무 살이 돼요.
examples.en: My daughter turns twenty next year.
My younger sibling turns ten next year.
What's your dream? — I want to become a teacher.

explain: 되다는 ‘이/가 되다’로 써요: 의사가 되다. 되 + 어요는 ‘돼요’로 써요. ‘되요’는 틀려요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 좋은 소식을 듣고 기뻐해 주는 말
phrases.nuance_en: said to share someone's joy after hearing good news

dict_examples.ko: 학교 갈 나이가 다 된 조카.
dict_examples.en: A nephew who is old enough to go to school.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: The child has turned five.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: It has been a year since we met.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: I want to become a doctor when I grow up.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: 되다 takes 이/가: 의사가 되다 (become a doctor). 되 + 어요 is written 돼요; “되요” is wrong.

examples.en: It's raining. Take an umbrella with you.

examples.ko: 저는 지금 돈을 조금 가지고 있어요.
examples.en: I have a little money with me now.
Did you bring your passport?
I'll bring my Korean book tomorrow.

explain: 가지다는 ‘가지고 가요/와요’처럼 무엇을 들고 갈 때 많이 써요. 말할 때는 ‘가져가요, 가져와요’로도 줄여요. ‘가지다’만으로 ‘have’를 말하는 일은 적어요. ‘차가 있어요’라고 해요.

dict_examples.en: My younger sibling went to school with a ball.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: How much money do you have?
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: What is that you're holding in your hand?
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: He goes to the study to get a book.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: 가지다 is mostly used as 가지고 가요/와요 (take/bring). In speech it shortens to 가져가요/가져와요. For “have”, Koreans usually say “차가 있어요”, not 가지다.

dis.h: full form; works before vowel endings
gh: short form; only before consonant endings

examples.en: Grandma's kimchi stew is special.
Today is special.
This place's sauce is really special.
What's special today? — The dessert.
This hanbok has a special color.

explain: 특별하다는 보통 좋은 느낌으로 다르다는 뜻이에요. 이상하게 다를 때는 ‘특이하다’를 써요.

dict_examples.en: A special feeling.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 철수는 영이에게 특별한 관심을 갖고 있었다.
dict_examples.en: Cheolsu had a special interest in Yeong-i.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 박 여사의 말대로 아침 커피의 향기는 특별했다.
dict_examples.en: As Mrs. Park said, the aroma of the morning coffee was special.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: 특별하다 means different in a good, special way. For different in a strange way, use 특이하다.

examples.en: I buy clothes at Dongdaemun.
Shops in Dongdaemun stay open until late at night.

examples.ko: 동대문 시장은 몇 시에 문을 열어요?
examples.en: What time does the Dongdaemun market open?

explain: 동대문은 원래 서울 성의 ‘동쪽 큰 문’이라는 뜻이에요. 지금은 밤에도 쇼핑하는 옷 시장으로 유명해요.
explain_en: 동대문 originally means the “East Great Gate” of old Seoul's wall. Today it is famous for its clothes markets that stay open at night.

examples.en: I catch the plane at Incheon.
Incheon is next to Seoul.
Incheon has the sea.
I'm meeting my friend at Incheon Airport.
I go from Incheon to Seoul. I take the subway.

explain: 인천공항은 서울이 아니라 인천에 있어요. 서울에서 공항철도로 한 시간쯤 걸려요.
explain_en: Incheon Airport is in Incheon, not in Seoul. It takes about an hour on the airport railroad from Seoul.

examples.en: I will meet my friend at the bus terminal.

examples.ko: 버스 터미널에서 부산 가는 버스를 타요.
examples.en: I take the bus to Busan at the bus terminal.
I bought a ticket at the terminal.
The terminal is next to the subway station.
I wait for my friend at the terminal.
I take a taxi in front of the terminal.

explain: 한국에서 터미널은 보통 버스 터미널이에요. 기차를 타는 곳은 ‘역’이라고 해요.

dict_examples.en: A transfer terminal.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: The terminal's last bus time.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 출발하기 전에 터미널에서 간단히 식사를 하기로 했다.
dict_examples.en: We decided to have a quick meal at the terminal before departing.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 터미널은 버스 이용객 말고도 배웅하거나 마중 나온 사람들로 항상 북적거린다.
dict_examples.en: The terminal is always crowded not only with bus passengers but also with people seeing off or picking up others.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: In Korea 터미널 usually means a bus terminal. Where you take a train is called 역 (station).

examples.en: The scenery I saw from the mountain was really nice.
The view here is really nice.
I look at the view from the top of the mountain.
This restaurant has a really nice view.
How's the view? — Very nice.

explain: 경치는 보통 ‘좋다’와 같이 써요: 경치가 좋아요. 높은 곳에서 보는 경치는 ‘전망’이라고도 해요.

phrases.example: 경치가 좋아도 금강산도 식후경이니까 먼저 밥 먹어요.
phrases.en: The view is great, but food comes first, so let's eat.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아무리 좋은 것도 배가 고프면 즐길 수 없음
phrases.nuance_en: a proverb: even the best things can't be enjoyed when you're hungry
phrases.en_equiv: The view is great, but food comes first, so let's eat.

dict_examples.en: The scenery is good.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: The scenery is outstanding.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 이 산은 빼어난 경치를 자랑하고 있다.
dict_examples.en: This mountain boasts outstanding scenery.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: 경치 usually goes with 좋다: 경치가 좋아요. The view from a high place is also called 전망.

dis.h: a beautiful view you enjoy looking at

p.n: 경치 stresses the beauty of the view; 풍경 is a more neutral scene.

examples.en: Jeju is an island.
My grandmother lives on a small island.
I want to live on an island for a month.

examples.ko: 섬에 가고 싶어요? — 네, 배를 타고 싶어요.
examples.en: Do you want to go to the island? — Yes, I want to take a boat.
Korea has many islands.

explain: 섬 이름 뒤에는 보통 ‘-도’가 붙어요: 제주도, 거제도, 울릉도. ‘제주섬’이라고는 잘 안 해요.

dict_examples.ko: 바다 한가운데에 외로이 떠 있는 섬.
dict_examples.en: An island floating lonely in the middle of the sea.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 남해는 크고 작은 섬이 많아 다도해라 불린다.
dict_examples.en: The South Sea has many large and small islands, so it is called an archipelago.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 이 다리는 섬과 육지를 이어 준다.
dict_examples.en: This bridge connects the island and the mainland.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: Island names usually end in -도: 제주도, 거제도, 울릉도. People rarely say “제주섬”.

examples.en: After work I had a glass of soju with a friend.
How about a glass of soju after so long?
I introduced soju to my foreign friend.

examples.ko: 한국 식당에서 소주는 보통 작은 잔에 따라 마셔요.
examples.en: In Korean restaurants, soju is usually poured into small glasses.
The soju glass is small, so it empties quickly.

examples.ko: 삼겹살을 먹을 때 소주 생각이 난다고 아버지가 말했어요.
examples.en: My father said he thinks of soju when he eats pork belly.

explain: 한국을 대표하는 술 중 하나로 보통 '한 잔', '한 병'으로 세요. 맥주와 섞은 것은 '소맥'이라고 해요. 어른과 함께 마실 때는 술을 두 손으로 받는 예절이 있어요.

phrases.en: I drank a bottle of soju with my friend.
I drink soju with my family on weekends.
phrases.nuance_ko: 술을 마신다고 할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for drinking alcohol.

phrases.en: I drank soju mixed with beer with my friends.
phrases.nuance_en: A drink made by mixing soju and beer.

explain_en: It is one of Korea's best-known drinks and is counted as '한 잔' (a glass) or '한 병' (a bottle). Soju mixed with beer is called '소맥'. When drinking with elders, there is an etiquette of receiving the drink with both hands.

examples.en: I add a little vinegar to cold noodles.
I wipe the window with vinegar.
I bought a bottle of vinegar.
The vinegar is too sour.
I sprinkle olive oil and vinegar on the salad.
The vinegar smell was strong, so I opened the window.

explain: 맛은 '시다'로 말해요. 줄여서 '초'라고도 하고 '초고추장'은 고추장에 식초를 넣은 소스예요. 요리뿐 아니라 청소에도 쓰는 사람이 많아요.

phrases.en: I put vinegar in the salad.
phrases.nuance_ko: 요리할 때 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase when cooking.

phrases.en: I eat naengmyeon with a little vinegar added.
phrases.nuance_ko: '식초'를 줄인 말이에요. 말할 때 편하게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A short form of 'sikcho', used casually in speech.

phrases.en: Please add one spoonful of vinegar to the water.
phrases.nuance_ko: 양을 말할 때 '한 숟가락'처럼 단위를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add a unit like 'han sutgarak' to say the amount.

explain_en: Its taste is described with '시다' (sour). It is sometimes shortened to '초', and '초고추장' is red pepper paste mixed with vinegar. Many people use it for cleaning as well as cooking.

examples.en: I bought 20 kilograms of rice.
I wash the rice to cook it.
We've run out of rice, so I have to go to the supermarket.
The price of rice went up a lot this year.
I make rice cakes from rice.
This rice is delicious.

explain: 익히기 전은 '쌀', 익힌 것은 '밥', 논에서 자라는 식물은 '벼'예요. 쌀은 '씻다', '떨어지다'와 자주 같이 써요.

phrases.en: I wash the rice before cooking.
phrases.nuance_ko: 밥을 지을 때 먼저 하는 일이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The first step before cooking rice.

phrases.en: We've run out of rice, so I'm going to buy some.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the rice has run out.

phrases.en: Today I ate white rice with kimchi.
phrases.nuance_en: Cooked rice made only from rice.

explain_en: Before cooking it is '쌀', cooked it is '밥', and the plant growing in the paddy is '벼'. '쌀' often goes with '씻다' (wash) and '떨어지다' (run out).

examples.en: I went to bed late last night.
My husband is coming home late today.
Yesterday's meeting ended late.
I got up late this morning. I was very busy.
I came late. I'm sorry.

explain: 반대말은 “일찍”이에요. 일찍 자요 ↔ 늦게 자요. “빨리”의 반대말은 “천천히”예요.

phrases.ko: 늦게 배운 도둑이 날 새는 줄 모른다
phrases.example: 늦게 배운 도둑이 날 새는 줄 모른다더니 요즘 게임에 빠졌어요.
phrases.en: someone who starts something late gets more absorbed in it
phrases.nuance_en: used about someone who starts late but gets even more absorbed than others
phrases.en_equiv: someone who starts something late gets more absorbed in it

explain_en: The opposite is 일찍: 일찍 자요 (go to bed early) ↔ 늦게 자요. The opposite of 빨리 is 천천히.

examples.en: There was leftover kimchi in the fridge, so I made kimchi fried rice.

examples.ko: 김치볶음밥에 계란 프라이를 올려 먹으면 맛있어요.
examples.en: Kimchi fried rice is tasty with a fried egg on top.
For lunch I want to eat kimchi fried rice.

examples.ko: 김치볶음밥은 만들기 쉬워서 자주 해 먹어요.
examples.en: Kimchi fried rice is easy to make, so I cook it often.

examples.ko: 친구가 만든 김치볶음밥 맛이 정말 좋았어요.
examples.en: The kimchi fried rice my friend made tasted really good.

examples.ko: 여기요, 김치볶음밥 하나랑 라면 하나 주세요.
examples.en: Excuse me, one kimchi fried rice and one ramyeon, please.

explain: 김치를 넣고 볶은 밥이에요. 집에서는 '만들다'나 '해 먹다'를 쓰고, 식당에서는 '시키다'나 '주문하다'를 써요. 새우볶음밥, 야채볶음밥처럼 앞에 재료를 붙여 다른 볶음밥도 말할 수 있어요.

phrases.en: I ordered kimchi fried rice at the restaurant.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when ordering food at a restaurant.

phrases.en: I made kimchi fried rice for lunch.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집에서 직접 만들어 먹을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you make and eat it yourself at home.
phrases.en_equiv: to make and eat kimchi fried rice

phrases.en: One bowl of kimchi fried rice, please.
phrases.nuance_ko: 식당에서 양을 말하며 주문할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to state the amount when ordering at a restaurant.
phrases.en_equiv: a bowl of kimchi fried rice

explain_en: It is fried rice stir-fried with kimchi. At home people say '만들다' or '해 먹다', and at a restaurant '시키다' or '주문하다'. You can put other ingredients in front, as in 새우볶음밥 or 야채볶음밥, to name other fried rice dishes.

examples.en: I eat lunch at a restaurant near my office.
What did you eat for lunch today?

examples.ko: 동생이 점심밥을 먹고 바로 학교에 갔어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling ate lunch and went straight to school.

examples.ko: 점심밥 먹을 시간도 없을 만큼 바빴어요.
examples.en: I was so busy I didn't even have time for lunch.
I brought gimbap for lunch.

examples.ko: 학교 점심밥이 맛있어서 한 그릇 더 먹었어요.
examples.en: The school lunch was tasty, so I had another bowl.

explain: 보통은 그냥 '점심'이라고 하고, '점심밥'은 밥 먹는 것을 조금 더 구체적으로 말하는 편한 표현이에요. 격식 있게는 '점심 식사'라고 해요. 싸 가지고 가는 점심은 '도시락'이라고 해요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 조금 격식 있게 말할 때 써요.

phrases.en: I brought a packed lunch today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집에서 싸 가지고 가는 점심을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A lunch you pack at home and carry with you.

explain_en: People usually just say '점심', and '점심밥' is a casual way to talk about the meal more concretely. The formal version is '점심 식사'. A packed lunch you carry along is called '도시락'.
